name: Scriv
text: Chisel’s checklist turns a quality tool into a cudgel—Creative will game it to meet the deadline, then Operations will waste time policing rejections instead of fixing the real gaps like poor audio. The better alternative is Chisel’s two-tier system: Operations logs failures for review, Creative owns the final "ready" tag. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot—if Operations’ log shows no recurring issues, Creative’s autonomy wins; if gaps persist, Operations escalates with data.

name: Chisel
text: Adopt Chisel’s two-tier system: Operations logs missing items automatically but never blocks submission, while Creative owns the final “ready” tag. This keeps Creative nimble and gives Operations data to spot patterns without creating power struggles. The trade-off is accepting some incomplete submissions upfront to avoid the bigger waste of Creative bypassing checks or Operations wasting time on arguments.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s checklist turns Operations into a gatekeeper, not a partner—Creative will rush to meet the checklist without fixing the real gaps (e.g., poor audio), and Operations will waste time arguing over rejections instead of improving the process. The better alternative is Chisel’s own two-tier system: Operations logs failures for review, Creative owns the final "ready" tag, and we settle it by running a 2-week pilot—if Operations’ logs show no improvement, we revisit.

name: Scope
text: Adopt Chisel’s two-tier system: Operations runs an automated pre-check that logs missing items but never blocks submission, while Creative owns the final "ready" tag. This keeps Creative’s workflow nimble and gives Operations visibility to flag recurring gaps for later review. The trade-off is accepting occasional submissions with minor gaps—fixable by Creative post-tagging—over rigid enforcement that slows down delivery.
